@dataclass
class User:
    """Represents a registered user of the application.

    A ``User`` holds identity and account state, along with the set of items
    the user owns. It exposes small helpers for the two predicates the rest
    of the codebase needs: whether the user is allowed to log in, and
    whether the user owns a particular item.

    Attributes:
        id: Unique integer identifier for the user.
        email: The user's email address. Used both as a contact handle and,
            via :meth:`can_login`, as a minimal sanity check for login
            eligibility.
        name: Human-readable display name for the user.
        active: Whether the account is currently enabled. Inactive users
            cannot log in regardless of their email.
        item_ids: List of item IDs owned by the user. Defaults to an empty
            list for newly created users.

    Methods:
        can_login: Return ``True`` when the account is active and the email
            looks superficially valid.
        owns_item: Return ``True`` when the given item ID is in
            ``item_ids``.

    Example:
        >>> user = User(id=1, email="ada@example.com", name="Ada")
        >>> user.can_login()
        True
        >>> user.item_ids.append(42)
        >>> user.owns_item(42)
        True
        >>> user.owns_item(7)
        False
    """

    id: int
    email: str
    name: str
    active: bool = True
    item_ids: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)

    def can_login(self) -> bool:
        """Return whether this user is permitted to log in.

        A user can log in when their account is ``active`` and their
        ``email`` contains an ``@`` character. The email check is
        intentionally minimal; stricter validation lives in the
        validators module.

        Returns:
            ``True`` if the user is active and their email contains
            ``"@"``; otherwise ``False``.
        """
        return self.active and "@" in self.email

    def owns_item(self, item_id: int) -> bool:
        """Return whether this user owns the given item.

        Args:
            item_id: The integer ID of the item to check.

        Returns:
            ``True`` if ``item_id`` appears in :attr:`item_ids`;
            otherwise ``False``.
        """
        return item_id in self.item_ids

    """Represents a registered user of the application.

    A ``User`` holds identity and account state, along with the set of items
    the user owns. It exposes small helpers for the two predicates the rest
    of the codebase needs: whether the user is allowed to log in, and
    whether the user owns a particular item.

    Attributes:
        id: Unique integer identifier for the user.
        email: The user's email address. Used both as a contact handle and,
            via :meth:`can_login`, as a minimal sanity check for login
            eligibility.
        name: Human-readable display name for the user.
        active: Whether the account is currently enabled. Inactive users
            cannot log in regardless of their email.
        item_ids: List of item IDs owned by the user. Defaults to an empty
            list for newly created users.

    Methods:
        can_login: Return ``True`` when the account is active and the email
            looks superficially valid.
        owns_item: Return ``True`` when the given item ID is in
            ``item_ids``.

    Example:
        >>> user = User(id=1, email="ada@example.com", name="Ada")
        >>> user.can_login()
        True
        >>> user.item_ids.append(42)
        >>> user.owns_item(42)
        True
        >>> user.owns_item(7)
        False
    """

    id: int
    email: str
    name: str
    active: bool = True
    item_ids: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)

    def can_login(self) -> bool:
        """Return whether this user is permitted to log in.

        A user can log in when their account is ``active`` and their
        ``email`` contains an ``@`` character. The email check is
        intentionally minimal; stricter validation lives in the
        validators module.

        Returns:
            ``True`` if the user is active and their email contains
            ``"@"``; otherwise ``False``.
        """
        return self.active and "@" in self.email

    def owns_item(self, item_id: int) -> bool:
        """Return whether this user owns the given item.

        Args:
            item_id: The integer ID of the item to check.

        Returns:
            ``True`` if ``item_id`` appears in :attr:`item_ids`;
            otherwise ``False``.
        """
        return item_id in self.item_ids
